5th-class-maths-book.subject: Mathematics
description: Mathematics is an important subject that helps students develop logical thinking, problem-solving abilities and numerical skills. A good understanding of basic mathematical concepts makes it easier for students to learn advanced topics in higher classes.

The Class 5 Maths Book introduces students to different mathematical concepts through examples, activities and practical exercises. Students learn about numbers, fractions, geometry, measurements, patterns and data handling.

CBSE 5 Class Maths  designed to make mathematics more interesting and understandable. With regular practice and proper study materials, students can improve their mathematical knowledge and develop confidence in solving questions.

sections.heading: Understanding the Class 5 Maths Textbook
paragraphs: The Class 5 Maths Textbook introduces students to mathematical concepts that are useful in everyday life. It encourages students to understand concepts instead of simply memorising formulas.
The current NCERT textbook is called Maths Mela. It includes activity-based learning and practical examples that connect mathematics with real-life situations.
Students can use their Maths for Class 5 to understand concepts, practise exercises and develop a strong foundation in mathematics.

sections.heading: Important Topics Covered in Class 5 Mathematics
paragraphs: The NCERT Class 5 Maths Book covers different topics that help students improve their mathematical understanding.

subsections.heading: 1. Numbers and Calculations
paragraphs: Students learn about large numbers, place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. These concepts improve calculation skills and numerical understanding.

subsections.heading: 2. Fractions
paragraphs: Fractions help students understand parts of a whole. Students learn how to identify, compare and work with fractions through different examples.

subsections.heading: 3. Geometry and Shapes
paragraphs: Geometry introduces students to different shapes, angles, patterns and symmetrical designs. These concepts help develop spatial understanding.

subsections.heading: 4. Measurement
paragraphs: Students learn about length, weight, capacity and different units of measurement. These concepts are useful in everyday activities.

subsections.heading: 5. Time and Data Handling
paragraphs: Students understand time calculations, reading information from tables and interpreting data through pictures and charts.

structure-of-atom-class-11.subject: Chemistry
description: Chemistry is an important subject for students in Class 11, as it introduces several fundamental concepts that help build a strong understanding of science. One of the important topics in Chemistry is the structure of atoms.

Structure of Atom Class 11 explains how atoms are organised and how subatomic particles such as electrons, protons and neutrons contribute to atomic structure. This chapter introduces students to different atomic models, quantum numbers, electronic configuration and atomic orbitals.
The Class 11 Chemistry Chapter 2 helps students understand the basic principles of atomic structure and provides a foundation for learning advanced chemistry concepts.

sections.heading: What Is Structure of Atom?
paragraphs: An atom is the basic unit of an element that retains its chemical properties. It consists of three main subatomic particles: electrons, protons and neutrons.
Understanding atomic structure helps students learn how elements behave and how chemical reactions take place.
list: Protons: Positively charged particles present in the nucleus.
Neutrons: Particles without an electric charge, present in the nucleus.
Electrons: Negatively charged particles associated with the space around the nucleus.

sections.heading: Important Topics Covered in Structure of Atom Class 11
paragraphs: Class 11 Chemistry chapter covers several important concepts related to atomic structure.

subsections.heading: 1. Discovery of Subatomic Particles
paragraphs: Students learn about the discovery of electrons, protons and neutrons. This topic explains the basic composition of an atom and the properties of its particles.

subsections.heading: 2. Atomic Models
paragraphs: Different scientists proposed atomic models to explain the structure of atoms.
Important atomic models include:
These models explain how scientific understanding of atomic structure developed.
list: Thomson's Atomic Model
Rutherford's Atomic Model
Bohr's Atomic Model

subsections.heading: 3. Bohr's Atomic Model
paragraphs: Bohr's model explains the arrangement of electrons in specific energy levels around the nucleus. Students learn about energy levels, electron transitions and the hydrogen spectrum.

subsections.heading: 4. Quantum Mechanical Model
paragraphs: The quantum mechanical model provides a modern explanation of electron behaviour in atoms. It introduces orbitals and the probability of finding electrons in different regions.

subsections.heading: 5. Quantum Numbers
paragraphs: Quantum Numbers describe the position and properties of electrons in an atom.
There are four types:
list: Principal Quantum Number
Azimuthal Quantum Number
Magnetic Quantum Number
Spin Quantum Number

subsections.heading: 6. Electronic Configuration
paragraphs: Electronic configuration explains how electrons are distributed among different shells and orbitals of an atom.
Students learn three important principles:
These principles help students understand the arrangement of electrons in different elements.
list: Aufbau Principle
Pauli Exclusion Principle
Hund's Rule

Understanding these formulas helps students solve numerical problems and improve conceptual clarity.

Students who understand atomic structure can develop better conceptual knowledge and improve their ability to solve chemistry problems.

sections.heading: Chapter-Wise NCERT Solutions for Class 9 Maths
paragraphs: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics covers 12 core chapters that introduce students to fundamental mathematical concepts:

Number Systems, Polynomials, Coordinate Geometry, Linear Equations in Two Variables, Introduction to Euclid's Geometry, Lines and Angles, Triangles, Quadrilaterals, Circles, Heron's Formula, Surface Areas and Volumes, and Statistics.
list: Chapter 1: Number Systems – Real numbers, rationalisation, and laws of exponents
Chapter 2: Polynomials – Factorisation, algebraic identities, and zero of a polynomial
Chapter 3: Coordinate Geometry – Cartesian plane, coordinates of a point, and quadrants
Chapter 4: Linear Equations in Two Variables – Solutions and graphical representation
Chapter 5: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry – Definitions, axioms, and postulates
Chapter 6: Lines and Angles – Vertically opposite angles, transversal lines, and angle sum
Chapter 7: Triangles – Congruence criteria (SAS, ASA, AAS, SSS, RHS) and properties
Chapter 8: Quadrilaterals – Properties of parallelograms and mid-point theorem
Chapter 9: Circles – Chords, arcs, subtended angles, and cyclic quadrilaterals
Chapter 10: Heron's Formula – Area of triangles and application in quadrilaterals
Chapter 11: Surface Areas and Volumes – Cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, and spheres
Chapter 12: Statistics – Graphical representation of data, bar graphs, and histograms

sections.heading: Importance of NCERT Solutions for Class 9 Maths

Exam-Oriented Practice: Gain confidence tackling various question formats, from MCQs to multi-step descriptive problems.

Maintain a dedicated formula notebook for quick revision before exams. Practise solving NCERT textbook examples before attempting exercise questions. Dedicate extra time to geometry proofs and algebraic factorisation, as these areas require precision and regular practice.

sections.heading: Importance of Objective Questions in Class 10 Maths
paragraphs: Objective questions test quick thinking and exact concept application without lengthy derivations. Consistent practice of MCQs helps students in several key ways:
list: Speed and Time Management: Solving 20 one-mark questions accurately in the first 30–35 minutes leaves ample time for Section B, C, D, and E.
Concept Precision: Objective questions often test boundary conditions, properties, and definitions where precision matters.
Elimination Techniques: Learn how to eliminate incorrect options using estimation, parity checks, and substitution.
Formula Recall: Reinforce direct formula application across coordinate geometry, trigonometry, arithmetic progressions, and probability.

sections.heading: Chapter-Wise Topics for Class 10 Maths Objective Questions
paragraphs: Explore the key objective question patterns across major units:
list: Real Numbers: HCF and LCM relationship (HCF × LCM = a × b), terminating/non-terminating decimal expansions, and irrationality conditions.
Polynomials: Sum and product of roots (α + β = -b/a, αβ = c/a), number of zeroes from graphs.
Pair of Linear Equations: Conditions for consistency (unique solution, infinitely many solutions, no solution).
Quadratic Equations: Nature of roots using discriminant D = b² - 4ac (real and distinct, equal, or no real roots).
Arithmetic Progressions: Finding common difference d, nth term a_n = a + (n-1)d, and sum S_n.
Coordinate Geometry: Distance formula, section formula coordinates, midpoint formula, and distance from origin.
Introduction to Trigonometry: Values of standard trigonometric ratios (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°) and basic Pythagorean identities.
Statistics & Probability: Empirical relationship (3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean), class marks, and probability of complementary events P(E) + P(not E) = 1.

faqs.q: How many objective questions are asked in CBSE Class 10 Maths board exam?
faqs.a: Section A of the CBSE Class 10 Maths board question paper contains 20 objective questions (18 multiple choice questions and 2 assertion-reason questions), each carrying 1 mark.

faqs.q: What is the best strategy to solve Maths MCQs in board exams?
faqs.a: Read the question carefully, check units, eliminate obviously incorrect options, use substitution or graphical inspection where applicable, and avoid rough work errors.

faqs.q: Are assertion-reason questions included in Class 10 Maths?
faqs.a: Yes, questions 19 and 20 in Section A are typically assertion-reason questions testing deep conceptual comprehension.

sections.heading: Chapter-Wise Breakdown of Class 10 Science
paragraphs: The CBSE Class 10 Science curriculum is organized into Chemistry, Biology, and Physics units:
list: Chemical Reactions and Equations: Types of chemical reactions (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox), balancing equations, corrosion and rancidity.
Acids, Bases and Salts: Properties, pH scale, preparation and uses of Bleaching Powder, Baking Soda, Washing Soda, and Plaster of Paris.
Metals and Non-Metals: Physical and chemical properties, reactivity series, ionic compounds, extraction of metals, and prevention of corrosion.
Carbon and Its Compounds: Covalent bonding, versatile nature of carbon, homologous series, functional groups, and chemical reactions of ethanol and ethanoic acid.
Life Processes: Nutrition, respiration, transportation in plants and animals, and excretion in human beings.
Control and Coordination: Nervous system, reflex arc, human brain structure, plant hormones (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid), and animal hormones.
How do Organisms Reproduce?: Asexual and sexual reproduction, reproductive health, contraceptive methods, and flowering plant reproduction.
Heredity: Mendel's experiments, laws of inheritance (monohybrid and dihybrid cross), and sex determination in human beings.
Light – Reflection and Refraction: Spherical mirrors, mirror formula, magnification, refraction through glass slab, lens formula, and power of a lens.
The Human Eye and the Colourful World: Eye defects (myopia, hypermetropia, presbyopia) and corrections, refraction through prism, dispersion, and atmospheric refraction.
Electricity: Electric current, potential difference, Ohm's law, resistance factors, series and parallel resistor combinations, heating effect of electric current, and electric power.
Magnetic Effects of Electric Current: Magnetic field lines, Right-Hand Thumb Rule, force on current-carrying conductor, Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, and domestic electric circuits.
Our Environment: Ecosystem components, food chains, food webs, 10 percent energy flow law, ozone layer depletion, and waste management.

sections.heading: Why Are NCERT Solutions for Class 10 Science Important?
paragraphs: CBSE board examination question papers are framed directly around NCERT textbook exercises, in-text questions, and exemplar problems. Thorough preparation using these solutions guarantees maximum coverage of exam concepts.
list: Accurate Chemical Equations: Master balanced symbol equations and reaction conditions required by CBSE marking schemes.

faqs.q: Are NCERT solutions sufficient for scoring 95+ in Class 10 Science?
faqs.a: Yes. NCERT textbooks are the primary reference for CBSE board exams. Mastering all in-text questions, chapter-end exercises, and activities covers over 90% of exam questions.

faqs.q: How important are diagrams in Class 10 Science?
faqs.a: Diagrams carry significant weightage in Biology (human heart, excretory system, neuron) and Physics (ray diagrams, electric circuits, magnetic field lines). Clean, labeled diagrams earn full marks.

faqs.q: How many chapters are in Class 10 Science?
faqs.a: The CBSE rationalised syllabus for Class 10 Science includes 13 chapters across Chemical Substances, World of Living, Natural Phenomena, Effects of Current, and Natural Resources.

sections.heading: Three Main Branches of Class 12 Chemistry
paragraphs: The CBSE Class 12 Chemistry syllabus is divided into three major branches, each demanding a distinct preparation strategy:
list: Physical Chemistry: Focuses on numericals, formulas, and laws. Key chapters: Solutions, Electrochemistry, and Chemical Kinetics.
Inorganic Chemistry: Emphasizes electronic configurations, oxidation states, periodic trends, and coordination complexes. Key chapters: d- and f-Block Elements, and Coordination Compounds.

Organic Chemistry: Centers around named reactions, reaction mechanisms, functional group interconversions, and biomolecules. Key chapters: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes, Alcohols Phenols and Ethers, Aldehydes Ketones and Carboxylic Acids, Amines, and Biomolecules.

sections.heading: Chapter-Wise Highlights in Class 12 Chemistry
paragraphs: Important topics covered across the 10 prescribed CBSE units:
list: Solutions: Raoult's Law, colligative properties (relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure), van 't Hoff factor, and ideal/non-ideal solutions.
Electrochemistry: Nernst equation, standard electrode potentials, Kohlrausch's law, molar conductivity, Faraday's laws of electrolysis, and battery types.
Chemical Kinetics: Rate of reaction, rate law and order, integrated rate equations for zero and first order reactions, Arrhenius equation, and collision theory.
d- and f-Block Elements: Transition metals properties, variable oxidation states, lanthanoid contraction, and preparation of K2Cr2O7 and KMnO4.
Coordination Compounds: Werner's theory, IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, Valence Bond Theory, Crystal Field Theory, and magnetic properties.
Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: SN1 and SN2 reaction mechanisms, optical rotation, and electrophilic substitution reactions.
Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation methods, acidic nature of phenol, Kolbe's reaction, Reimer-Tiemann reaction, and Williamson ether synthesis.
Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Nucleophilic addition mechanisms, Aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, and acidity of carboxylic acids.
Amines: Basicity of amines in aqueous and gas phase, Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, Hofmann bromamide degradation, and diazotisation.
Biomolecules: Classification of carbohydrates, glucose structure, peptide linkage in proteins, primary/secondary/tertiary structures, DNA/RNA structures.

sections.heading: CBSE Class 7 Maths Syllabus and Chapters
paragraphs: The NCERT Class 7 Mathematics curriculum covers the following key chapters designed to advance numerical and geometrical reasoning:
list: Integers: Properties of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of integers (closure, commutative, associative, and distributive properties).
Fractions and Decimals: Multiplication and division of fractions and decimals, real-life applications in measurements and money.
Data Handling: Collection and organization of data, arithmetic mean, median, mode of ungrouped data, and constructing bar graphs.
Simple Equations: Setting up equations, solving linear equations by balancing and transposing methods.
Lines and Angles: Complementary and supplementary angles, adjacent angles, linear pairs, vertically opposite angles, and angles formed by parallel lines cut by a transversal.
The Triangle and its Properties: Medians, altitudes, exterior angle property, angle sum property, and Pythagoras theorem in right-angled triangles.
Comparing Quantities: Ratios, percentages, converting decimals/fractions to percentages, profit and loss calculations, and simple interest (I = PRT/100).
Rational Numbers: Positive and negative rational numbers, representation on number lines, equivalent rational numbers, and arithmetic operations.
Perimeter and Area: Squares, rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, and circles (circumference = 2πr, area = πr²).
Algebraic Expressions: Terms, factors, coefficients, monomials, binomials, trinomials, polynomials, like and unlike terms, addition and subtraction of algebraic expressions.
Exponents and Powers: Laws of exponents (a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m / a^n = a^(m-n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn)), expressing large numbers in scientific standard form.
Symmetry: Lines of symmetry for regular polygons, rotational symmetry, order of rotational symmetry, and center of rotation.

sections.heading: Chapter-Wise NCERT Solutions for Class 10 Maths
paragraphs: The commonly listed NCERT Class 10 Maths chapters include the following 14 chapters:
list: Chapter 1: Real Numbers – Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, proving irrationality of √2, √3, √5, and prime factorisation.
Chapter 2: Polynomials – Geometrical meaning of zeroes, relationship between zeroes and coefficients of quadratic polynomials.
Chapter 3: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables – Graphical method, substitution method, elimination method, and consistency conditions.
Chapter 4: Quadratic Equations – Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, factorisation method, quadratic formula, and discriminant nature of roots.
Chapter 5: Arithmetic Progressions – General term a_n = a + (n-1)d, sum of first n terms S_n, and everyday word problems.
Chapter 6: Triangles – Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' theorem) and its converse, criteria for similarity of triangles (AAA, SSS, SAS).
Chapter 7: Coordinate Geometry – Distance formula, section formula (internal division), and midpoint formula.

Chapter 8: Introduction to Trigonometry – Trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot) of acute angles, standard angle values (0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°), and trigonometric identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
Chapter 9: Some Applications of Trigonometry – Heights and distances, angles of elevation and depression, single and double triangle word problems.
Chapter 10: Circles – Tangent to a circle at point of contact, theorem proving tangents drawn from external point are equal in length.
Chapter 11: Areas Related to Circles – Sector and segment areas, arc lengths, and composite plane figure areas.
Chapter 12: Surface Areas and Volumes – Combinations of cubes, cuboids, spheres, hemispheres, and right circular cylinders/cones.
Chapter 13: Statistics – Mean, median, and mode of grouped data using direct and assumed mean methods.
Chapter 14: Probability – Classical definition of probability, simple events, and complementary events.

Comprehensive coverage of all exercise questions and examples leaves no topic unpractised.

faqs.q: Are NCERT solutions enough to score 100 in Class 10 Maths?
faqs.a: NCERT textbook questions and exemplar problems form the core of the CBSE Class 10 Maths board exam. Practising all exercises along with sample papers and past year papers ensures top performance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Maths Basic and Maths Standard in Class 10?
faqs.a: Both courses share the exact same NCERT syllabus and textbooks. Maths Basic examination questions test direct concepts and simple calculations, while Maths Standard includes more analytical and multi-step problem-solving.

faqs.q: Which units carry the highest marks in Class 10 Maths?
faqs.a: Algebra (20 marks) and Geometry (15 marks) carry the highest marks, followed by Trigonometry (12 marks) and Statistics & Probability (11 marks).
